correctness.rationale: The two-component ideal differences force y=0 and xz=0, so singularities occur only at [1:0:0] and [0:0:1]. Local branches have expansions z=-a y^2. Any embedded analytic isomorphism preserves the unique common tangent; its 2-jet Y=alpha*y+beta*z+..., Z=delta*z+gamma*y^2+... yields b=(delta*a-gamma)/alpha^2, an affine action. Conversely Y=y, Z=uz-vy^2 realizes all affine changes, preserving the transverse y=0 line. A global projectivity sends the conic span <xz,y^2> to itself, preserving its unique rank-one and rank-two singular members and therefore acts on the parameter by scaling only. Symbolically checked determinant -lambda^2*mu/4, affine identity, and explicit translated but non-scaled triple. The proof covers all m>=3, not merely the witness.

value.rationale: An extremal global Tjurina/freeness classification does not determine global projective equivalence even after all embedded local analytic germ types are fixed. The explicit degree-six/seven witnesses and exact fiber dimension provide a structural obstruction to recovering global geometry from local singularities, motivating the precise invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter substitution.

final_claim: For m>=3 smooth conics xz+a y^2 with distinct nonzero complex a, the two singular embedded analytic germs of C_A and line-added D_A depend on A up to affine transformations a->ua+v, whereas global projective equivalence is exactly scaling a->ca. Generic dimensions of the respective moduli are m-2 and m-1; A={1,2,4}, B={2,3,5} witness equal local analytic types and unequal global projective types.
